record_type_quote: The objective of this study is to replicate the fourth experiment conducted by Sperling in 1960 which examined the duration of information in brief visual presentations.

targets.title: The information available in brief visual presentations.
targets.evidence_quote: The objective of this study is to replicate the fourth experiment conducted by Sperling in 1960 which examined the duration of information in brief visual presentations.
targets.outcome_quote: In contrast, one of our results differs from what Sperling observed: the ascending or descending order in which the sound instruction is presented does not significantly affect participants’ performance. This difference may be explained by the fact that Sperling only examined the effect of order when the stimuli were presented as two rows of letters.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The discussion explicitly agrees with the original delay effect but contrasts the instruction-order finding and capacity findings. The abstract support statement concerns partial-report accuracy rather than an unqualified verdict over the whole replication.

reasoning: Identity and author list verified on publisher page and complete eleven-page article. One published original is explicitly retested using a new participant sample.
